 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition(Civil) No. 931/2025
 Sarbjeet Kaur Petitioner(s)
 Versus
 Pradeep Kumar Respondent(s)
 O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The parties are also present before the Court in-person, identified by their learned counsel.
3. At the outset, we have been informed that in Mediation the parties have settled the matter and a joint application has been filed by them.
4. The terms of the settlement have also been stated in the affidavit.
However, the settlement of Agreement is being reproduced for the sake of ready reference.
SETTLEMENT AGGREEMENT

This Settlement Agreement is executed on 08th September, 2025 at New Delhi between Sarbjeet Kaur, W/o Mr. Pradeep Kumar, D/o- Sh.
Puranchand, R/o - Village Jhotan Tehsil and District Fazilka, Punjab (hereinafter referred to as FIRST PARTY) AND Mr. Pradeep Kumar, S/o Sh.
Satnamchand, R/o Manewala, Tehsil Suratgarh, District Sriganga Nagar, Rajasthan (hereinafter referred to as SECOND PARTY).
WHEREAS marriage between the first party and the second party was solemnized on 29.01.2023 in accordance with Hindu Rites, Customs and Ceremonies at Preet Palace, Arniwala, Fazilka.

AND WHEREAS the parties had thereafter stayed together as husband and wife upto January,
2024, after which matrimonial disputes arose between them.
The parties started living separately.
There is no issue out of this wedlock.

AND WHEREAS the first Party had then instituted Transfer Petition (C) No. 931 of 2025 before the Honble Supreme Court of India.
At the joint request of the parties referred the parties for mediation before the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.

Comprehensive mediation sessions were held with the parties on 28.07.2025, 05.08.2025, 13.08.2025, 28.08.2025 and today i.e. 08.09.2025 both the parties physically present before the Mediation Centre.

AND WHEREAS after discussions and negotiations held between the parties during the mediation proceedings, the parties have arrived at an amicable settlement wherein, they have agreed to settle all their disputes on the following terms: -
1. The Parties agree that the marriage between them has irretrievably broken down due to irreconcilable differences and that it shall not be possible for them to stay together as husband and wife.
2. That the Parties agree that they shall file appropriate application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India before the Honble Supreme Court, seeking mutual consent divorce and disposal / quash of abovesaid cases.

3. In consideration of the above, second party agrees to pay a lump-sum of Rs.
7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Only) to the first party as full and final settlement of all her claims past, present and future and towards all her claims arising from/out of such marriage including alimony, stridhan and maintenance etc.
4. That the Second Party shall hand over Demand Draft of Rs. 7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Only) to the First Party within 3 months from the signing of the present settlement agreement.

5. That it is agreed between the parties that the Second Party shall have no objections if the gold jewellery lying in the custody of the Ld. Judicial Magistrate First Class-2, Fazilka, Punjab is released in favour of the First party.

6. It is further agreed between the first party and the second party that all the cases filed by them, if any, and or at the instance shall be withdrawn by them.
7.

It is agreed between the parties that they will strictly adhere to the terms and conditions of this settlement agreement and will do all acts and sign all the relevant documents required for the purpose of obtaining divorce by consent.

8. Both the parties have executed this settlement agreement before the Mediator appointed by Supreme Court Mediation Centre of their own accord and free will, without perpetration of any force undue influence or coercion and both the parties shall be estopped in law to assail the validity of any clause/terms of the present settlement agreement on the ground of being void and unlawful.

Further the parties have confirmed and undertaken that they were given sufficient time and opportunity to consult their legal counsels and it is only after said consultations and full understanding of the effect of the terms and conditions of the present settlement agreement, the parties have executed the present settlement agreement.
9. That both the parties are well qualified and have perused and understood the contents of the present settlement agreement.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF both the parties have signed this settlement agreement in the presence of the mediator at New Delhi on 08th day of September, 2025.
5. The affidavit reveals that they have settled to withdraw/seek quashing/disposal of all civil and criminal proceedings, details of which have been given at paragraph No.7(d)of the affidavit.
It has further been prayed that the Court may exercise its jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and grant divorce through mutual consent to the parties.
6. We have interacted with the parties and are satisfied that they have settled the matter in mediation of their own free will without any coercion or duress.

7. Learned counsel for the respondent, in terms of the settlement, hands over a demand draft of Rs.
7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs) in favour of the petitioner-wife bearing no.
496167 dated 17.01.2026 payable in the name of Sarbjeet Kaur D/O. Puran Chand, which is accepted by her.
8. The cases mentioned in paragraph No.7(d) of the affidavit stand quashed.
Further, exercising our jurisdiction/powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, the parties are granted divorce on the ground of mutual consent.
9. Registry is directed to draw the decree accordingly.
